about.defining: AssureProof keeps the source page with every figure. A language model writes the draft from those files. A formal consistency checker tests whether the draft's figures and the locked source values can all be true at the same time. Red-Hat review is a separate language-model pass that tries to find what is wrong in that draft, and it runs only when someone asks for it. A person decides.
about.diff.2.name: The formal consistency checker tests the figures.
about.diff.2.text: A formal consistency checker tests whether the draft's figures conflict with the values locked from the source. The language model does not make that call for a labeled figure.
about.diff.3.name: Red-Hat review is a second reading.
about.diff.3.text: Red-Hat review is a language-model pass on the draft, and it runs only when someone asks for it. It tries to find a mismatch, an overstatement, a missing clause, or a figure that needs a citation.

about.title: About AssureProof
about.what.body: AssureProof is a platform that checks a draft against the files it was written from, before you pay or sign off. If an invoice is over the contract cap, or a claim doesn't match the policy, you see the mismatch on the review screen with both source pages open. A person decides whether each flagged figure is right. AssureProof runs inside your own environment.
about.who.1: Finance: catch supplier invoices that go over contract caps or agreed terms before the payment run, with the contract page open next to the invoice.
about.who.2: Claims: catch claim figures that don't match the policy or the supporting documents before the payout.
about.who.3: Procurement: catch bids and supplier packs that don't meet the tender requirements before award.

faq.1.a: AssureProof reads your PDFs and scans. When you ask for a draft, it writes one from those files, checks the draft against what it read from your files, and shows the figures and statements that don't match what the files say. A person reviews each flag and decides. It runs in your own AWS account or on your own servers.
faq.10.a: Yes. Bring a real document set for one workflow. We agree a fixed scope in writing, run it with your team and walk you through the findings. Use the contact form or write to sales@assureproof.com.
faq.10.q: Can I try it on my own files?
faq.2.a: Extraction tools read data out of a file and return fields. RAG tools answer questions and cite sources. AssureProof writes a draft from your files and then shows where that draft conflicts with them, so a reviewer sees the mismatches before the draft is approved, paid or sent.
faq.2.q: How is AssureProof different from extraction tools and RAG tools?
faq.3.a: Z3 is software that decides whether a set of figures can all be true at the same time. AssureProof uses it on the figures and dates in a draft. A language model writes the relation, such as "the invoice total is at most the contract cap", and Z3 checks it against the values read from your files. Each check reports pass, fail, skipped, timeout or error.
faq.4.a: It means the figure check gives the same answer each time for the same figures and the same relation. Reading the files and writing the draft are done by language models, and a model writes the relation that is checked, so those steps can vary. That is why a person reviews each flag before anything is approved.
faq.5.a: No. Z3 checks figures and dates where a relation can be written. Statements are judged by a language-model support check against the cited source. Each draft claim must cite a source, page and field, or a quote, and a citation that does not resolve fails the claim. A skipped or errored check is never reported as a pass.
faq.5.q: Does AssureProof check every statement in the draft?
faq.6.a: Red-Hat review is a second language-model pass that runs on every draft and on each document's fields. It looks for weak claims, such as an overstatement or a figure that needs a citation, and lists them with reasons. It does not block anything. A person decides what to do with each one.
faq.7.a: No. AssureProof marks the contradiction and a person decides. A reviewer can accept a value over a Z3 or Red-Hat review objection, and that decision is recorded with who made it and when. You can export fields as CSV or JSON, with the JSON signed so it can be verified, and drafts as JSON or PDF.
faq.8.a: ParSure reads PDFs, including scans, and PNG, JPEG, TIFF and BMP images, up to 25 MB and 200 pages per file by default. Handwritten and illegible values are flagged, and illegible values are not guessed. CrossSure reads spreadsheets in XLSX, XLSM, XLS, CSV and TXT formats without a model.
faq.9.a: Runs in your own AWS account or on your own servers, including air-gapped networks; model calls go to your Amazon Bedrock account (or a self-hosted model on a GPU). Files are stored on your own disk or in your S3 bucket. With a self-hosted model, document text stays inside your environment. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
faq.a1: AssureProof reads your contracts, invoices, claims and bids together and marks every figure that does not match across them, with both source pages open. A person reviews each flag and decides. It runs in your own AWS account or on your own servers, including air-gapped networks.
faq.a2: Z3 is a formal logic solver (SMT solver) that mathematically proves whether a set of figures and constraints can all be true at the same time. The figure check itself is deterministic: the same figures and rules always give the same answer.
faq.a3: The figure check itself is deterministic: the same figures and rules always give the same answer. Reading the documents and drafting use language models, so every figure keeps its source page for a person to confirm. If the figures conflict today, they will conflict tomorrow.
faq.a4: A separate adversarial pass in which a language model tries to find flaws in the draft — missing citations, overstated claims, or numbers that do not trace back to a source page. The Red-Hat review is configured per customer deployment: it can run on every draft or only when a reviewer requests it.
faq.a5: No. AssureProof marks the contradiction and a person decides. A reviewer can accept a value over a Z3 or Red-Hat review objection, and that decision is recorded with who made it and when. You can export fields as CSV or JSON, with the JSON signed so it can be verified, and drafts as JSON or PDF.
faq.a6: In your own AWS account (using Amazon Bedrock), on a private GPU, or on your own on-premises servers — including air-gapped networks. You choose the deployment model; documents never leave your boundary unless you connect an external endpoint yourself.

landing.why.copy: Generative AI is fast, but it is fundamentally unverified. In enterprise compliance, guessing is a liability. AssureProof AI places a deterministic verification engine between your models and your output. It checks math with formal logic, tracks source provenance down to the exact page, and flags every logical gap before a human ever has to look twice.

sec.1.body: In your own AWS account, on-premises, or private GPU environment. You choose where the models run, and the deployment stays inside your network boundary. Nothing is shared with other tenants, and the infrastructure stays under your control.
sec.1.title: Where it runs
sec.2.body: Local: documents stay inside your environment, and nothing leaves it. Hosted: customer data is never used for training. With a local model, documents do not leave your boundary at any point in the check.
sec.2.title: Model boundary
sec.3.body: Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.3 and at rest with AES-256. Each check keeps its own review record, kept under your retention settings, with the source page linked to every figure.
sec.3.title: Encryption
sec.4.body: Every user signs in. Each project is visible only to its owner and the people they add. Access can be reviewed and revoked by your own administrators at any time.
sec.poc.body: Every POC runs in an isolated single-tenant environment. Your documents are never retained or used to train or fine-tune AI models — zero AI model training — and are deleted after the review according to the agreed retention.

terms.accuracy: AI systems are probabilistic and can hallucinate. Verification is a filter, not a promise of accuracy. We do not promise that output is flawless, complete, or free from errors. Independently verify critical information.
terms.advice: AssureProof performs document analysis, verification, and compilation. It does not give legal, financial, or professional advice. Consult qualified professionals before you act on any output.
terms.answers: AssureProof rewrites your question, can send it to models you connect, and can drop claims that were not in your files. That is a filter, not a promise of accuracy. You check the result before you use it with a client, a paper, or a decision.
terms.as_is: The software is provided "as is", without warranties. We are not liable for damages or other consequences of your use. We do not promise uptime, accuracy, or fitness for a particular job. Any service levels are set only in your signed enterprise agreement.
terms.duty: You are solely responsible for how you use AssureProof. You agree not to use it for any unlawful, harmful, or abusive purpose.
terms.files: Only upload files you have the right to use. Do not upload privileged, confidential, or sensitive information unless you are authorised to do so. Do not send health or other sensitive text to a provider that is open to the internet unless you mean to. We are not responsible for uploads that violate your own obligations.
terms.indemnity: You cover losses that arise from your use of AssureProof. Our total liability is capped at the amount you paid for the service. We are not liable for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages.
terms.law: You are responsible for how you use the output. If these terms cannot be enforced in your location, the rest still apply.
terms.lead: How AssureProof works, what you are responsible for, and what we do not promise.
terms.prohibit: You may not use AssureProof to generate or promote:
terms.prohibit.rights: Content that violates the rights of others
terms.providers: You must also follow the terms of the AI provider you connect. A Send to a connected provider is subject to that provider's rules. AssureProof does not replace them.
terms.send: AssureProof keeps the source page with every figure and shows the contradiction before you pay. A person decides. The file can still be downloaded. Runs in your own AWS account, on-premises, or private GPU environment. You choose where the models run.
terms.third: We are not liable for decisions made by third parties who rely on the output. Do not share output with others without your own verification.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.use: AssureProof is designed for document compilation, verification, and compliance review. It is not a substitute for binding legal, financial, or regulatory decisions. If you rely on the output as your sole verification, that responsibility stays with you.
terms.verify: You are solely responsible for verifying outputs before you take action. AssureProof is an aid to human judgment, not a replacement for it. Human review is mandatory before you rely on any document.
terms.where: AssureProof runs in your own AWS account, on a private GPU, or on your own servers, including air-gapped networks. why_not_llm.sub: ChatGPT and Claude are built to sound plausible, not to guarantee mathematical consistency across a 300-page document stack. When a missed clause or billing overage costs thousands of dollars, probability is not enough.
why_not_llm.table.cta.text: Use LLMs to brainstorm. Use AssureProof before you sign, pay, or file.
why_not_llm.table.rows.audit.assure: Full governance trail recording every flagged conflict, reviewer sign-off, and override.
why_not_llm.table.rows.audit.llm: No built-in approval gates or cryptographic audit log of who overrode a discrepancy.
why_not_llm.table.rows.conflict_handling: Automatically locks export upon disagreement, forcing a human decision.
Quietly smooths over contradictions to give you a polite, confident answer.
why_not_llm.table.rows.core_engine.assur: Deterministic — mathematically tests every figure and rule using a Z3 formal logic solver.
why_not_llm.table.rows.core_engine.llm: Probabilistic — guesses the most likely text based on patterns.
why_not_llm.table.rows.math.assure: Z3 checks whether every figure, clause, and citation can all be true at the same time. A contradiction stops export.
why_not_llm.table.rows.math.llm: Often misses subtle discrepancies or loses accuracy as file length grows ("lost in the middle").
why_not_llm.table.rows.residency.assure: Runs 100% inside your AWS account, private GPU, or air-gapped on-prem server.
why_not_llm.table.rows.residency.llm: Prompts and files typically pass through third-party cloud APIs.
why_not_llm.table.rows.traceability.assu: Every claim is pinned directly to the exact source document, page, and line.
why_not_llm.table.rows.traceability.llm: Citations can be vague, paraphrased, or fabricated.
